hypothesis.text: If artificial intelligence and automation create economic output increasingly independent of human labor, Constitutional Capitalism can keep the resulting surplus broadly distributed—so abundance increases human freedom rather than concentrating economic power—by broadening ownership of productive capital (retirement, employee, cooperative, community, Prosperity Fund, local enterprise, citizen investment vehicles) while protecting innovation incentives and recognizing dual claims: private returns for genuine innovation and a societal interest in sharing extraordinary productive returns built on humanity's accumulated knowledge and publicly supported infrastructure.
hypothesis.central_question: If artificial intelligence and automation create economic output increasingly independent of human labor, what ownership, market, community and public-capital structures allow the resulting surplus to remain broadly distributed among the people and communities whose accumulated knowledge, institutions and infrastructure helped make that productivity possible?
hypothesis.philosophical_objective: The goal is not to redistribute scarcity forever. It is to build institutions capable of distributing the benefits of abundance.

scarcity_assumption_shift.today_implicit: How does Arkansas finance abundance while economic output is constrained by human labor?
scarcity_assumption_shift.ai_problem: What happens when productive capacity grows much faster than the amount of human labor required to produce it?
scarcity_assumption_shift.today_chain: human labor → production → wages → consumption → taxes → public services
scarcity_assumption_shift.automation_chain: capital + AI + energy + data → enormous production → relatively little labor → returns concentrate around ownership
scarcity_assumption_shift.implication: Successfully retraining everybody can still confront an economy that does not need everyone's labor in historical quantities

hypothesis.objective_lock: Use technology to eliminate scarcity while distributing the productive benefits of technology broadly enough that abundance increases human freedom rather than concentrating economic power.

governance.reason: Registered under CC-DEC-141. CC-DEC-142 locks parallel evidence-only posture: do not expand HYP-134 until transition-indicator series are bound; must not contaminate today’s fiscal math or rescue the Replacement Stack by assumption.

hard_walls: AI abundance is a hypothesis, not a forecast
Projected productivity is not replacement-stack revenue
Collective intellectual inheritance does not mean government ownership of private innovation
Automation gains should not automatically accrue exclusively to capital owners
Broad ownership is preferred over permanent dependency
Local/community retention is measured, not assumed

dual_legitimate_claims.private: Private innovators deserve returns for creating genuinely valuable technology — capital, engineering, research, risk, infrastructure
dual_legitimate_claims.social: Society has a legitimate interest in sharing in extraordinary productive returns generated from humanity's accumulated knowledge and publicly supported infrastructure

critical_variable.name: ownership
critical_variable.prefer: Own part of the productive economy
critical_variable.demote_as_primary: Giant AI tax as sole strategy — avoidance risk; residual wealth taxes remain available as last-resort instruments
critical_variable.stronger_long_run: As labor becomes less necessary for production, broaden ownership of the capital doing the producing

concentrated_abundance.owners: Small number of companies own AI + robots + energy + data + logistics + IP

distributed_abundance.chain: AI productivity → enterprise earnings → distributed ownership returns → household wealth + community wealth + Prosperity Fund returns

prosperity_fund_pathway.prior_modeling_bias: Fund contributions modeled almost entirely as money that must first be raised
prosperity_fund_pathway.ai_abundance_pathway: Arkansas accumulates productive ownership before the abundance transition fully arrives
prosperity_fund_pathway.implication: If the Prosperity Fund owns diversified productive assets, increased AI productivity can increase public income — without counting projected AI boom as COUNTABLE NOW

community_ai_ownership.illustrative_case_not_locked: Food-processing cooperative deploys AI/robotics, doubles output, needs 30% fewer labor hours
community_ai_ownership.conventional: automation → fewer workers → higher owner margins
community_ai_ownership.cc_test: automation → higher productivity → worker/community ownership returns + lower prices + shorter work requirements + reinvestment
community_ai_ownership.rule: Do not predetermine exact percentages — test which structures work

concept_of_work.reject: A person has value only insofar as the market needs their labor
concept_of_work.if_machines_do_necessary_work: Civilization succeeded at producing more with less labor — people have not become worthless
concept_of_work.desired_path: less compulsory labor → more civic time → stronger communities
concept_of_work.failure_path: less employment → poverty → dependency → social collapse

education_join.not_only: What job are we training this child to perform?
education_join.increasingly: What capabilities allow this person to create, own, govern, adapt and contribute in a society where machines perform increasing amounts of routine economic production?
education_join.shift: Less worker factory; more human-capability system
education_join.note: Does not expand HYP-133 operating passes — join note only until Demand Map empirical build

ai_productivity_transition_dashboard.purpose: Empirical warning indicators rather than assuming abundance arrives

replacement_stack_role.rule: Do not inflate demoted Base@16y (~$840M ceiling) because we imagine an AI boom

separate_scenario.name: AI_Abundance_Sensitivity
separate_scenario.question: If AI produces substantially higher productivity and capital returns while reducing labor requirements, how would different ownership structures distribute that surplus?

defining_idea_candidate.statement: If AI changes production as profoundly as contemplated, the economic philosophy designed for the next century cannot assume that human labor will forever remain the scarce input around which society organizes income, dignity, taxation and ownership.

linked_hypotheses.HYP-126: Distributed civic commons — more discretionary time can strengthen civic society
linked_hypotheses.HYP-129: Local proof sites for ownership structures
linked_hypotheses.HYP-131: Prosperity Fund ownership pathway; residual wealth last resort; stack sensitivity only
linked_hypotheses.HYP-132: Retain/attract people and capital in an ownership society
linked_hypotheses.HYP-133: Human-capability education for abundance economy — join note only

lane_posture.role: Important enough to shape later modeling; isolated enough that it cannot contaminate today’s fiscal math
lane_posture.then_allowed: Compare ownership structures under AI-abundance sensitivity model
lane_posture.key_distinction: AI abundance may change the long-run economics of Constitutional Capitalism, but it does not rescue today’s replacement stack by assumption.
lane_posture.anti_rescue_rule: HYP-134 cannot become the convenient answer whenever current revenue math fails. If AI-driven abundance eventually materializes, the evidence will tell us when the underlying economic assumptions have changed.

pre_transition_baseline.purpose: Establish an AI transition baseline before the transformation occurs — so later we can say what changed, where, who captured gains, who lost income/bargaining power, and whether CC institutions kept prosperity distributed locally
pre_transition_baseline.timing: Next major HYP-134 empirical pass — data-heavy baseline bind — only after main External Income evidence work is underway; modeling later

research_gate: Dashboard / ownership comparison / sensitivity modeling may begin only after transition-indicator series are bound — not before
